title: Paul G NDE 665
content:
I was in a three-day summer camp with my older brother (the one that died). There was a swimming pool there, so he decided to teach me to swim. When he had given me some fundamentals to work with, he told me to stay in the shallow water, and close to the edge. He then got out, and went to play with the roller skaters. It couldn't have been more than five minutes of practice, before I decided to combine techniques and swim across the pool! I made it halfway, about eight feet. In my desperation, after struggling for what seemed like forever, I did what they do in the cartoons. I stuck my hand out of the water, and lowered my fingers, one at a time. When I lowered them all, I let out my toxic air, with great relief. They said that when they rescued me, I was lying on the pool floor. They thought I was playing! So, they waited for me to come up for air! When I didn't, one of the counselors dove in after me. No one knows how long I was there before being spotted! Lotta kids! It's been a long time ago - I have always said that I remember as if it was yesterday. Guess I'm gonna have to stop saying that. The experience itself is why I said that. I cannot remember if the figures faded in, or I opened my eyes. At any rate, I have never been faced with such brightness! It was like being in a room that was being lit by its personal sun, only brighter! I really don't remember the number odd figures I saw - I always followed my religious background and figured twelve - for a minute, these men just stared. Then the middle one (Peter) leaned forward and his face was inches away from mine. Then he began to slowly shake his head, 'No'. As he did this, the bright lights very slowly began to soften, and slowly began to fade into a mixture of white and powder blue. I should say it was so bright in there; it was in black and white! A bright light making all the people look like shadows. I could make out faces, especially the one that leaned toward me. But they were all in black and white! Anyway, as the white light began to fade, the number of people began to grow - at the same time, the shapes, or the heights were changing. Color in the people, trees, chairs, etc. Then, there I lay. In the middle of a circle of children and adults!

arrival.religious_figure_detail: The middle one is identified as "Peter" and shakes his head 'No'.
arrival.other_being_detail: Narrator describes "odd figures"/"men" who stared; later the number of people grew and included "children and adults" in a circle around him.

environment.environment_other_detail: Mentions a very bright room lit by its "personal sun"; initially black-and-white with people as shadows; light fades into white and powder blue; later there is color in "people, trees, chairs, etc."

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Drowning in a swimming pool at a summer camp while trying to swim across the pool.

person_demographics.religious_affiliation_detail: Mentions following his "religious background" and assuming "twelve" figures; identifies one as "Peter".

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Experience includes extremely bright light; figures/men including one identified as Peter; later a circle of children and adults around him; no tunnel/OBE described.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Narrative begins with drowning/rescue context, then sudden encounter with bright light and figures; transitions as the light fades and scene shifts to being surrounded by children and adults.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Visual transition described as extremely bright black-and-white silhouettes that gradually fade into white/powder blue and then full color; one figure ("Peter") leans close and shakes head 'No'.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “It was like being in a room that was being lit by its personal sun, only brighter!”; “Then the middle one (Peter) leaned forward and his face was inches away from mine. Then he began to slowly shake his head, 'No'.”; “I should say it was so bright in there; it was in black and white! A bright light making all the people look like shadows.”
